local_articles.title: Kimi Antonelli hits wall as George Russell takes pol for Azerbaijan GP
local_articles.snippet: Kimi Antonelli was left ruing an uncharacteristic error in qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which eliminated the championship leader in the first session after he hit a wall in Baku. His Mercedes team-mate George Russell claimed pole with a fine lap and will be in a strong position to make up ground in the title chase in Saturday’s race. Antonelli leads Russell by 81 points in the world championship and has won the last two races but sat disconsolately trackside after only 11 minutes of running on Friday in Baku, when he was a little too eager into the 90-degree left-handed turn one and clipped the barrier. He took damage to the track rod and a puncture, and while he attempted to bring the car home, he was told to park up by his race engineer, Pete Bonnington. “We can’t fix this, mate,” he said. local_articles.title: george russell takes pole for azerbaijan grand prix
local_articles.snippet: BAKU, Azerbaijan – Briton George Russell stormed to a dominant pole position in qualifying on Sept 25 for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix and saw his fading title hopes receive a much-needed boost from a crash for Mercedes championship-leading teammate Kimi Antonelli. The 28-year-old clocked a 1min 42.526sec lap around the 6km Baku street track, bettering his own previous benchmark by 0.5sec, to go 0.837 clear of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc. Australian Oscar Piastri was third for McLaren. Antonelli, who leads Russell by 81 points in the overall standings and came into the weekend gunning for his third successive win and ninth of the season, will start 16th after crashing out in the first phase of qualifying. local_articles.title: Verstappen denies Russell Azerbaijan practice clean sweep
local_articles.snippet: BAKU, Azerbaijan, Sept 25 - Four-times champion Max Verstappen denied Mercedes rival George Russell a clean sweep of practice for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix by going fastest for Red Bull in Friday’s final session ahead of qualifying. The Dutchman clocked a one-minute, 43.922 second lap in the closing minutes of the hour-long session to pip Russell by 0.099 seconds. Lewis Hamilton also pulled out a late flier to go third for Ferrari 0.111 seconds off Verstappen’s pace. Runaway championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who lost valuable track time to a hydraulics issue on Thursday, was fourth. Russell, who trails his 20-year-old Italian teammate by 81 points after 14 rounds, has looked dialled in all weekend. The 28-year-old was fastest in both sessions of running on Thursday and, until Verstappen’s late effort, had looked set to close out his domination of practice with another fastest effort. C

questions.title: Which city or region will the DOSB choose in 2026 to represent Germany in bidding for the 2036, 2040 or 2044 Summer Olympics?
questions.background: The DOSB is Germany's national Olympic committee. Its domestic candidate selection is separate from the International Olympic Committee's eventual decision on which country will host the Games.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The DOSB's official selection announcement, as confirmed by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the city or region officially selected during 2026 to represent Germany in bidding for the 2036, 2040 or 2044 Summer Olympics. This concerns Germany's domestic candidate selection, not the eventual international host selection. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the selected city or region.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-09-24 STRUCTURAL ELIMINATION: Berlin officially withdrew its BERLIN+ Olympic bid today at a press conference by Mayor Kai Wegner, Sports Senator Iris Spranger, and Olympic Commissioner Kaweh Niroomand (official Berlin.de press release, Tagesspiegel, Straits Times/AFP Sept 24), citing the loss of political stability after Die Linke's Sept 20 state election win and Berlin's distant 3rd-place score (74.64/100) in Tuesday's DOSB Evaluation Commission report. Zeroing out Berlin (0.01 -> removed completely), leaving a pure 100% two-candidate single-round secret ballot between Munich and Rhine-Ruhr (KolnRheinRuhr) at Saturday Sept 26's DOSB extraordinary general assembly in Baden-Baden (144 votes: 42 Olympic federations x 3 en bloc = 126, DOSB Presidium 10, Personal Members 8; 73 votes needed). DW (Sept 23) describes Munich as slight favorite ('leichter Favorit') based on its #1 DOSB evaluation score (87.03 vs 85.02, both 'sehr gut', 100/100 Stability, compact One-Village concept, Bavarian winter-sport federation bloc), while Rhine-Ruhr remains a formidable ~37% challenger (only 2.01 pts behind, 66% referendum approval across 15 NRW cities, strong summer-sport/NRW base, and shared Rostock-Warnemunde sailing venue with former Berlin+ partner Mecklenburg-Vorpommern). Normalizing our 62:37 ratio cleanly to Munich 0.63 / Rhine-Ruhr 0.37 (sum = 1.00).

questions.title: Which national team will win the England–Spain UEFA Nations League match at Wembley on September 19, 2026?
questions.background: The UEFA Nations League is a competition for European national teams.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : UEFA's official match result and contemporaneous reporting of the completed match. Resolution : Resolve to the national team declared the winner at full time in the September 19, 2026 fixture. If the match finishes level, resolve as Draw. local_articles.snippet: Rodri claim the Ballon d’Or that year, and he is again among the candidates to be named the world’s best player.
